rationale: C12 plausibly supplied concrete administrative machinery later adapted for Stevenson: access to foreign-intelligence information through the CIA coupled with an express restriction against disclosing classified material. The child replaces a standing presidential advisory board with a presidential candidate receiving periodic briefings, but retains the core access-and-secrecy structure. C20 and C22 share the periodic foreign-intelligence/CIA setting, though they provide weaker drafting parallels because they focus on institutional review and reporting rather than personal receipt and protection of intelligence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: periodic briefings on the international scene from a responsible official in the Central Intelligence Agency
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The President's Board shall conduct an objective review of the foreign intelligence activities of the Government ... [including] the quality of the foreign intelligence provided
shared_material.explanation: Both establish recurring access to foreign-intelligence material through a presidential arrangement centered on the CIA.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the information itself would be of a secret character and exclusively for your personal knowledge
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each member of the President's Board shall execute an undertaking not to reveal any classified information obtained by virtue of his service
shared_material.explanation: Both pair intelligence access with a specific personal nondisclosure restriction, a concrete and material structural parallel.
